claims.text: Standard-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a coarse lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
Rapid cooling immediately after casting followed by optimized short-duration annealing refines lamellar spacing relative to conventional processing.
Rapid cooling followed by optimized annealing improves FCC/B2 interfacial morphology.
A refined or hierarchical lamellar microstructure can enable simultaneous enhancement of strength and ductility in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Rapid cooling suppresses excessive microstructural coarsening by freezing in a fine-scale lamellar arrangement.
The subsequent controlled anneal relieves internal stresses.
The subsequent controlled anneal slightly coarsens the most critical interfaces.
Increased interface density strengthens the alloy.
The refined microstructure improves ductility by promoting more uniform plastic deformation.
The proposed treatment will increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength by approximately 15–25% relative to slow-cooled, standard-annealed material.
The proposed treatment will increase elongation by a percentage comparable to the predicted 15–25% strength increase.
Conventionally slow-cooled and standard-annealed eutectic HEAs have coarser lamellae and lower strength and ductility than material receiving the proposed treatment.
Lamellar eutectic HEAs can balance strength and ductility by combining a soft FCC phase with a hard BCC phase or intermetallic compound.
The proposed improvement is limited to eutectic HEAs with a well-defined dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
Alloys lacking distinct dual-phase structures or undergoing deleterious transformations during rapid cooling may not benefit from the treatment.
Cryo-rolling followed by annealing produces simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 relative to as-cast and cold-rolled-and-annealed material.
Cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 achieved a yield strength of 1437 ± 26 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1562 ± 33 MPa, and elongation of about 14 ± 1%.

Tailored thermomechanical processing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can generate an ultrafine duplex hierarchical microstructure whose mechanical response is associated with hierarchical constraint and microcrack arrest.

contradictions.description: The treatment is said to be applied under ambient conditions, while it explicitly includes annealing at an optimized temperature. This is inconsistent if 'ambient conditions' refers to treatment temperature rather than atmosphere or subsequent testing.
